title: AI brief for South African business, 2 July 2026
summary: Google Search upgrades with Gemini 3.5 Flash and AI agents, while Apple prepares to overhaul Siri with Google Gemini at WWDC. The US government prioritizes AI security and innovation, and the AI for Good Summit focuses on global AI standards. DeepSeek releases an open-weight frontier AI model, and enterprise AI agents shift to outcome-based pricing.

items.headline: Google Search upgrades with Gemini 3.5 Flash and AI agents
items.what: Google announced the integration of Gemini 3.5 Flash into Google Search, making it the default model in AI Mode globally. The Search box has been upgraded to support more intuitive queries.
items.soWhat: South African businesses should ensure their online content is optimized for AI-driven search to maintain visibility. This includes clear, structured information that AI can easily parse and cite.
items.relatedTitle: How to get found on AI search in South Africa

items.headline: Apple overhauls Siri with Google Gemini
items.what: Apple is set to announce a major overhaul of Siri at WWDC 2026, powered by a custom Google Gemini model. This marks a shift from OpenAI's exclusivity to a multi-model approach.
items.soWhat: South African businesses using Apple devices should prepare for more advanced Siri capabilities, which could enhance customer interactions and automation workflows.
items.relatedTitle: ChatGPT vs Gemini vs Perplexity for a South African business

items.headline: US government prioritizes AI security and innovation
items.what: The US government issued an executive order to promote AI innovation and security, focusing on modernizing systems and protecting intellectual property.
items.soWhat: While this is US-focused, South African businesses should monitor global AI regulations as they may influence local policies and compliance requirements.

items.headline: AI for Good Summit focuses on global AI standards
items.what: The AI for Good Summit, organized by the UN, aims to develop AI standards and policies to harness AI for solving global challenges.
items.soWhat: South African businesses involved in AI should stay informed about global standards, which could impact local AI deployment and ethical considerations.

items.headline: DeepSeek releases open-weight frontier AI model
items.what: DeepSeek released its R1 model, an open-weight frontier AI model that rivals top closed models like GPT and Claude in performance.
items.soWhat: South African developers and businesses can leverage this open model for cost-effective AI solutions, though local infrastructure may limit deployment.
items.relatedTitle: The AI benchmarks, explained for a normal person

items.headline: Enterprise AI agents shift to outcome-based pricing
items.what: AI agencies are moving from hourly billing to outcome-based pricing, charging for business impact rather than time spent.
items.soWhat: South African businesses considering AI automation should evaluate ROI carefully, as pricing models now focus on tangible results rather than hours.
items.relatedTitle: Is AI worth it for a South African business in 2026?
